newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed higher on nearby short-covering. December added $1.20 to close at $306.90 while March firmed 70 cents to close at $305.90. No significant rise is expected unless there is greater physical offtake.

In New York raw sugar futures ended higher across the board with front month March adding 5 points to close at 10.53 cents, while May closed 4 points higher at 10.58 cents/lb. The outer months added 5 to 6 points. The rise was mainly technical and as long as physical offtake remains slack, the market may have difficulties defending current levels.

DOMINICAN REPUBLIC - Low domestic production and higher consumption have forced the Dominican Republic to increase sugar imports. Sugar imports in December 1995 amounted to 39,649 tonnes, raw value, against nil in the corresponding period the previous year. This brought cumulative imports in the first two months of 1995/96 (November/December) up to 54,649 tonnes against nil in the like period the previous year.

Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 36,360 tonnes against 39,598 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in November/December 1995 were Mexico with 15,039 tonnes whites, Brazil with 14,001 tonnes and the U.S.A with 13,800 tonnes.

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar imports from third countries in September 1996 amounted to 89,834 tonnes which brought total imports in 1995/96 (October/September) up to 1.24 million tonnes against 1.36 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of origin in October/September 1995/96 were Mauritius with 493,261 tonnes raws against 442,355 tonnes, Fiji with 185,580 tonnes compared to 173,350 tonnes, Guyana with 139,296 tonnes, down from 151,230 tonnes and Jamaica with 125,227 tonnes compared to 141,326 tonnes.

Sugar exports to third countries in September 1996 amounted to 25,872 tonnes, up from 17,711 tonnes exported in September 1995. This brought total exports in October/September 1995/96 up to 324,415 tonnes, down from 465,621 tonnes in October/September 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in 1995/96 were Israel with 126,282 tonnes whites against 143,376 tonnes, Norway with 47,798 tonnes against 38,951 tonnes and Turkey with 18,706 tonnes, up from 2,305 tonnes.
